sponsor: Modelled on Cambridge APS / JDRF INSPIRED trial
description: Closed-loop (artificial pancreas) systems are the most advanced form of insulin delivery for T1DM. They automate basal insulin delivery based on continuous CGM readings. Pre-screening identifies T1DM patients with high glucose variability and frequent hypoglycaemia — the patients who benefit most from automated insulin management. This protocol is T1DM-only: T2DM patients rarely qualify because they retain endogenous insulin secretion that makes closed-loop dosing unpredictable.

inclusion_criteria.human_rationale: Closed-loop systems are designed for patients with absolute insulin deficiency (T1DM). The algorithm assumes all glucose excursions require exogenous insulin correction. In T2DM, residual beta-cell function and insulin resistance make closed-loop dosing algorithms unreliable and potentially dangerous. All major closed-loop trials (Cambridge HCL, JDRF INSPIRED, DCLP3) enrolled T1DM exclusively.

A Coefficient of Variation ≥ 36% is the international consensus threshold (Battelino et al., Diabetes Care 2019) for 'high variability'. Patients above this threshold are most likely to benefit from closed-loop automation because their glucose is inherently unpredictable and difficult to manage with fixed basal rates.

Frequent hypoglycaemia (< 70 mg/dL) is the key driver for closed-loop adoption. The automated system detects declining glucose trends and reduces insulin delivery proactively — preventing the next hypo. Patients with ≥ 3 hypo readings per day have documented hypoglycaemia burden.
Below the ADA T1DM target of ≥ 70% TIR — indicates the patient is not meeting glycaemic goals on current open-loop therapy and is a candidate for technological intensification.

notes: v2: Added diabetes_type == T1DM inclusion criterion. Based on Hovorka R et al., Closed-loop insulin delivery in suboptimally controlled type 1 diabetes (Cambridge trial); and Bergenstal RM et al., Threshold Suspend for Prevention of Hypoglycemia (ASPIRE-In-Home trial).
